title: The Most Important Aspect of Leadership: Passing It On
paragraphs: But I want you to be a different kind of leader. I want you to be a rare leader. I want you to be the kind of leader the world will never forget. You can actually achieve that if you grasp these two important elements. The power of guidance and succession. I call it "passing the torch". It took me most of my life to appreciate the value of this process of guidance and succession. There is a reason why we do not provide guidance. I will explain some of those reasons.

I have also come to appreciate that the greatest leadership work is mentoring. It is not the construction of a building. It's not about creating a program. It is not about building an institution. It's not even about exercising power. The greatest act of leadership is guiding someone. Or direct a few people to take your place. I want to start by asking a question. What is leadership? We see people with titles and people with positions.

People we claim are influential, and we strangely conclude that they should be leaders. Whether they are a politician, a priest, a clergyman, or a business leader in a company, we always assume that these people are leaders. But when you start studying leadership, you find it to be something unattainable, because leadership is really defined by your culture. So, it may not be true leadership, and we talked about that in our session this morning, that there is leadership, and there is true leadership.

I want to give you a definition that took me 32 years to write. One sentence took me 32 years to write. Here is the sentence. Leadership is the ability to influence others through inspiration born of passion and motivated by vision, born of conviction, and produced by purpose. I want to repeat this. It's a long definition, but it's important.

Because based on my research, experience, interviews with thousands of leaders, and also conducting research in the most important book in the world, the Bible, my conclusion is that every word in this sentence is essential to defining leadership. Leadership is, once again, the ability to influence others through inspiration. Inspiration stems from a person's passion. This passion is driven by a vision that the person has. That vision comes from a deep conviction that the person cultivates.

That conviction comes from a sense of purpose. All these elements are necessary for leadership to be genuine. If you want to become a strong leader in your life to influence the world before you leave, and this is possible, then you should turn this sentence around and start from the bottom. Because leadership is never something to be sought after. True leadership is the product of a process. In essence, leaders never seek to be leaders. Every true leader in history was initially a hesitant person.

They did not want to be leaders. So, here's the process. Turn it upside down. Start from the bottom. First, you must discover your sense of purpose. You must somehow meet yourself and your Creator, which will help you realize that you are not wrong. And that you were born to do something important. I call that original intent. Once you find that sense of purpose, it develops a deep conviction. Conviction is believing in your own importance. Conviction is crucial in the process of becoming a leader.

Conviction is what makes a leader see a vision. Because the faith that is born within that person begins to appear in the form of images. They begin to see a better future. Therefore, all true leaders walk around with a picture in their minds of a future that is better, greater, and nobler than the present. That vision makes them develop a passion. Now, passion is the leader's fuel. Because it is passion, a desire stronger than the threat of death.

All true leaders are individuals who are prepared to die for their convictions. I am not only talking about physical death, although that may be possible and necessary, but I am also talking about dying for things like fame. Death to the desire to gain everyone's approval. Even to the point of dying for the desire to be loved by your friends or family. You should give that up if your conviction is strong enough. This is why many great leaders actually lose their friends.

Because conviction becomes more important than their company. This is what makes them leaders. Passion, then, is what inspires people. Now, when people see your passion for something, you inspire them. Inspiring a person means giving them meaning in their life. You make them believe that they too have something important to do in life, and that they can join you in making a difference. Inspiration is crucial in leadership because inspiration is the opposite of manipulation.

Most of those you call leaders, according to my definition, may simply be professional manipulators. They manipulate your fears, your need for acceptance, your need for appreciation, they play with your feelings and arouse your emotions. These are not leaders. These are frauds. Deceptive people. They are like mind controllers. Some of them are in politics, and some of them are on the podiums. They are manipulators. They are not leaders. True leaders never manipulate. They inspire others.

Once you inspire people, they willingly hand over their power to you. Only then will they call you a leader. Therefore, a true leader never sought leadership. It happened automatically. This is why they are usually hesitant people. They really don't want to be in the spotlight. They often tend to retreat into the shadows. You almost have to push them to the front. In fact, most of the true leaders in history were forcibly brought out of the shadows by circumstances. They had to respond.

For this reason, when you find people who seek power, positions, and leadership influence, you should be suspicious of them. Be careful of them. If people are seeking power, they are not leaders. Leaders do not seek power. In fact, they are usually given power they never asked for. Because their pursuit of their passion is what propels them to a leadership position. Here's a man you know very well. I will show you how important it is to understand the leadership process.

Leaders are not people who have found something to live for. Rather, they are people who have found something to die for. The problem with our generation is that we don't want to die. We want to live. We want to live in a big house and also own a luxury car. We want a lot of money, and we want a lot of fame. We want to be in the spotlight. We want to be in the spotlight. We don't want to die for anything. Death is part of leadership.

Let's read a statement made by Nelson Mandela that reveals the nature of the man he was. He says: "I have said nothing except what I am prepared to live for, and if it is the will of God Almighty, then death in His cause." Abraham Lincoln said so. But look at what Nelson Mandela says decades later. "It is an ideal that I hope to live for and achieve, but if necessary, it is an ideal that I am prepared to die for." Don't they look identical? No wonder we can't forget either of them.

I remember reading and listening to the great speeches and sermons delivered by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. I bought all his sermons when I was here two years ago. I listened to them all. And I remember the moment I think he became a leader. Do you remember that I told you all that there is a moment when that happens? I believe that happened when he was in that small church when they threatened his life. They had already told him that if he went out that night, he probably wouldn't see the sunrise.

He went up to the podium, and I am sure that Mr. Young was present at that meeting. He made this statement. He said they threatened to kill me. They threatened to end my life. Then he said, "But that's no longer important." Now, this statement is a leadership statement. You are never a leader until it becomes unimportant to you. Because at that moment, you would have died. As long as it matters to you, you will never change the world. Jesus said it this way. He said, "He who seeks his life loses it.

But if you are willing to lose your life for me, what will you do? You will find it." This means they will never be able to erase you from history. We need to ask ourselves: "Am I doing something right now that I am prepared to die for?" If you haven't reached that stage yet, you're just a supervisor. Perhaps a manager with a prestigious title, nothing more. But you are not a leader yet, because leaders are people who have a relationship with death. They have found something more important than life.

What are the keys to true leadership? Write this down. First, conviction and passion. Be prepared to sacrifice. Again, those quotes. It embodies the spirit of conviction and passion. And a willingness to sacrifice. This is the essence of the philosophy of a true leader. They constantly live in a relationship with death. They think of their goal as more important than their personal safety. I have a story to tell. My story is not over yet. But I was threatened.

Look at this man’s picture on the screen in the PowerPoint presentation here. This man changed the world. He was only 4 feet 5 inches tall. He weighed 90 pounds. This is it. When he decided that he would not eat until his people were free. He starved himself to death. He was fighting the entire British Empire. With all their armies, ships, and weapons, this little Indian man destroyed them without firing a single shot. He fought them with unwavering conviction. Contentment. This is what leaders today lack.

They have very little conviction. Conviction means that my faith is so strong that I would rather die than give it up. They tried to force him to eat. But he refused to eat. And the great British Empire collapsed under the weight of this little man's conviction. That is why we can never forget Mahatma Gandhi. I wonder if we will remember you. You are not remembered for what you have achieved. Rather, it reminds you of what you survived. Leadership. When I first met this man, he changed my life, you know. Mr.

Nelson Mandela. That was at a private dinner. I wanted to tell this story because it changed me deeply. When I first shook his hand, look at me there as I shook his hand. When I shook his hand, I felt that his hand was like a rock. Solid. It piqued my curiosity. That was 30 days after his release from Robben Island prison. He flew to the Bahamas to meet our Prime Minister, who had been a friend of his while they were studying in London. They all became lawyers.

When he returned to his homeland, my prime minister returned to my country. They were both fighting the same monsters. Persecution at the hands of Europeans. In my country, we faced the same problem. We had a system of racial segregation. There was a wall built in the middle of my island that we could not cross without permission. We didn't have passports. We were not allowed to eat at certain restaurants or drink from certain water fountains. The same thing. I was born and that was still there.

There were schools that were off-limits to us. We were unable to join it. It was intended for eggs only. So, my prime minister returned home to fight this issue. Mr. Mandela went on to fight the same thing in South Africa. They were both fighting against oppression. My Prime Minister, who was Sir Linden Oscar Pendling at the time, a young lawyer, fought against the system of oppression. But what is astonishing is that 4% of white people controlled 95% of the land and the economy. We owned nothing.

4% of the population controlled the country. I remember when we held the elections, when they came back, they started demonstrating in the streets, stopped taxis, and tried to impose the election result. They drew the boundaries in a way that ensured they always won. How can 4% win an election? Corruption to the core. In the end, they shut down the entire country. Those few leaders who returned from university. They have completely shut down the country. They told people: "Don't go to work. Don't drive buses.

Don't use taxis. We have shut down the country." They were forced to make a change. When they finally decided to hold fair elections, it was clear. And so, our new prime minister became the leader of the party, and the first prime minister, while his friend was still in prison in South Africa. He was the one who stood up at the United Nations and demanded that man be released. He started inciting others, and they joined him.

When he got out of prison, his first trip was to the Bahamas to say to his friend, "Thank you." They invited 17 people to dinner. I was one of them. Can you imagine that? That was about 17 years ago. I remember entering the room, and people were lining up to meet Mr. Mandela, who had just been released from prison. I mean, history was walking on two legs. I shook his hand, and I remember the feeling of that hand, which was as hard as a rock, and I said: " My God, this man's hand is as hard as steel, as cement."

He looked at me and smiled because he saw my face and my reaction. He bowed, and I bowed, and I said, "Mr. President." We went and sat down. Almost after the meal was finished, he leaned towards the table. I was sitting three chairs away. He said, " Young man, are you alright?" I said, "Yes, sir." He said, "Are you sure you're okay?" I said, " Yes, sir." He said, "No, you're not okay." He is a good man. He said, "I suppose you're wondering why my hands are so hard. " I felt extremely embarrassed.

He said: "Let me tell you why my hands are so hard. Because for 25 years in prison, they gave me an axe and a rock. They told me: Your job is to break rocks. Break them into small rocks. And that's how my hands became so hard. That's all we did for 25 years. Break rocks. Because of my convictions. They offered me deals to get out of prison many times. I told them: 'No, I can't sell my convictions.'" "Give me the axe again." And he told me this story.

I began to cry because I was listening to a man who had been the president of the country. But we forget the rocks. He said, " That's why my hand is hard." My whole hand is just calloused. I left that dinner that night with a thought in my mind that I still carry with me. And that thought is: " God, make my hand tough." You want to be a leader? You have to pay a price. If you want people to like you, don't try to be a leader. If you want fame, don't try to be a leader.

If you want popularity, don't try to be a leader. That's what he told me that night, that statement. He said, " Real leaders don't chase after followers." Followers are drawn to true leaders. They are drawn to your passion.” He also reminded me that leadership is n’t truly the leader’s right. It’s a privilege bestowed by followers. So, leadership is a trust people give you because they are inspired by your willingness to die for your convictions.

They accept you because they believe you are willing to sacrifice for what you believe in. That is the essence of leadership. So, this is the greatest challenge of leadership. You are now a leader. You are in a position of influence. You have revealed your passion. People respect you. Now, what do you do? Well, as I said, it’s time to think about the future.

The greatest act of leadership is mentoring, because if what you have learned, achieved, accumulated, and accomplished dies with you, you are the failure of a generation. So, the goal of leadership is not to achieve greatness, but to successfully pass it on. Mentoring, then, is the embodiment of the highest maturity because it means you are essentially handing over everything you have worked for to someone else.

When you come from a background like most of us, we don’t want to give away what we have achieved to anyone because our history tells us it’s better to keep everything because you never truly owned anything. So, we don’t mentor people. We destroy them when they try to compete with us. We need to To remember that the low self-esteem that comes from our history and our poor self-concept is what actually made us protect ourselves from others instead of training them to replace us.

What we have is what we call the concept of entitlement. Entitlement means, "I have suffered for the past 400 years. Now it's my turn. I have a right to this. And no one will take it from me. Not even my cousin." That is the spirit of entitlement. Do you know why I consider Mr. Mandela the greatest leader of our century? Let me tell you why. He was imprisoned for 25 years. He became president of the country and only had one term left. That's unheard of for an African. Mr.

Mugabe, who is also an acquaintance of mine. How long was he in power? I forget. Of course, there are other issues surrounding that process, but if he had been smart, he would have trained younger men and women. For the past 20 years, with the same philosophy, to replace him so he could go play golf. But he never crossed that threshold that would allow him to relinquish power. Do you know that the average age of Third World leaders is... As they say, he's 69. At 70, it's time to leave. Average age.

In other words, these are people who cling to their positions because they equate their worth with their status. Please take note. It's a very important point. True leaders understand that leadership is never granted to one generation. Leadership that only serves its own generation is doomed to fail. That's why I'm so pleased when I see people like Ambassador Andrew Young documenting history for children yet unborn to remember. You have to pass on that information to give them a sense of what was achieved.

Do you know why your children paint graffiti on walls? They have no idea what that wall cost. And it's usually because you haven't told them the story. Do your high schools in low-income areas teach your history to children? If they don't, that's why they paint on walls. Because they don't appreciate the value of the wall. The wall means nothing to them. They've forgotten that blood bought that wall. But you don't tell them the story. You don't guide them.

Guidance is understanding that leadership is a process passed down through generations. I like this phrase. God is the God of generations. You know, as I read the Bible over the years, I finally understood God. When God speaks to you, He isn't speaking to you. He's speaking to your descendants. You have to study God. He is a generational thinker. Whenever God tells you something, it's not for you. It's for your children. God used to say things like, " I will bless you.

I will bless your children, and your children's children will be blessed." In other words, I'm not speaking to you now. So, you'd better hold onto what I give you because it's not for you. One of the most important things I 've discovered is that success without a successor is failure. Success is the only word in the dictionary that has " success" inside it. Can I say that again? Succession is the only word in the dictionary that has "success" inside it. That means the only true success is succession.

So, leadership can only be maintained if you can guide people to maintain what you've built. If your vision dies with you, you're a failure. As you strive to be a great leader and make the most of your life, you have to keep thinking, "I have to start passing this on." For others. One of the things I try to do is constantly guide people because buildings are going downhill. When I went to Haiti, I went to visit Haiti and, you know, we traveled there to meet the president. We went to see the president.

And when we entered the presidential compound, the building was destroyed. There was rubble everywhere. I mean, the presidential palace was rubble. And as we were driving there, I asked the driver, I said, " How old is it?" He said, "These buildings are over 125 years old." He said it only took 125 seconds to destroy it. An earthquake, you know, in Haiti destroyed it. And I walked inside that palace. We sat with the president. We had tea together. We talked about issues. And then we left and said goodbye to him.

We prayed with him. And on my way out, I was crawling over the rocks. Coming from the presidential palace. Over the rocks. And I heard a voice saying to me, "Do you see why you're guiding?" Don't build your future in buildings. It only takes one earthquake. Build your future in people. I saw people climbing over the rocks. I discovered that the buildings were destroyed, but the people were still alive. Jesus Christ never built a building. He built people. He left us with 11 men who changed history.

Who will you leave behind? What will you leave behind? Because "what" could be destroyed by a hurricane or storm. What about "who" will you leave behind? We need leaders who think about the next generation more than the next position. In other words, we need leaders who feel they owe it to the future. And not just for the past. We need leaders who are more dedicated to history than they are to money. Oh, my God. You are a shepherd. Some of you here are shepherds.

Who are you training now to replace you on the podium? I discovered something. If you are not a guide, you will not be able to go on vacation. It's that simple. You are so selfish, self-obsessed, and insecure that you cannot take a vacation. Why? Because you don't trust anyone to stand on your pulpit. O shepherd. You are sick. Great leaders like to give up power. They like to see their students outperform them. We need history more than money.

Ladies and gentlemen, we need leaders who care more about people than their own ambitions. This is my service. This is my position. This is my company. This is my wipe. This is mine, mine, mine. These are sick people. These are not leaders. These are parasites. They suck the blood of people's trust to build their personal ambition. Leadership is not about your personal ambition. It's about people getting what they truly deserve. That's why you should be a guide. Ladies and gentlemen, remember this.

The biggest weakness in leadership is the lack of guidance. I want you to be wise. I want you to go out from here to your departments and find three people to mentor over the next four years. The fourth point is very important. The greatest fear of leadership is the success of followers. You know, some people are so afraid of their followers surpassing them that they eliminate their followers.

You know, I have actually seen pastors go on a break and leave the church in the hands of another pastor, a young pastor or something like that. And when they return, the whole church is talking about that young shepherd. Oh shepherd, you should have been here. It was wonderful. He sold more records than you did. Oh shepherd, I am very glad that you traveled. We have finally had the opportunity to hear a word from God. I mean, Brother John was brilliant, my shepherd. Thank you for allowing him to preach.

Oh shepherd, that was amazing. Now the shepherd is having some problems. That was the last time John would preach. Its cylinders are pulled from the department. She says, "Don't preach again." Because you are a sick leader. Your response should have been like Jesus'. Let me give you the mindset of Jesus as a leader. Here is his way of thinking, his philosophy. He said, "It is better for you that I go." Yes! Because he says, "Unless I go forth, you will not do greater works than I have done." This man is crazy.

He is actually telling them: "I am standing in your way." What do you think about telling your youth sponsor about that? He says, "It's better for you if I go." Because if I do not go, you will not accomplish greater things. My absence is important to you. What a leader's mindset. So, what he did was send them two by two. Do you remember that? They did something. They began by casting out demons, healing the sick, and raising the dead. You know, he gave them the authority to exercise all that power.

When they returned, they began to submit their report. They said, “Teacher, even the demons are afraid of us, the dead are raised, and the blind see.” He began to tell them, you know, if this had been a preacher from Atlanta, he would have said, “This is the last time I am sending you.” Do you know what the Bible says about what Jesus did? He says: "At that moment, Jesus rejoiced." The word "tahlil" means joy, and it means jumping for joy. Meaning that he jumped around him. Yes! Peter, give me "five", man.

I did it. John! He was excited because they performed better than he did. What a leader. They applauded him. He is not like you. Do not be afraid of the success of your followers. Be proud of him. And if you are smart, do what I do. Take credit for yourselves. Come on, clap again. Say, "This is my boy. This is my boy. I trained him. Look how clever he is! Look at that girl. That's my girl, man. I trained her." Take credit for yourselves. Don't be jealous. Take credit for yourselves. Do you know what we do?

We discourage people. You're not giving them any chance. This is the problem. If you discourage people, you have to stay with them to keep them down. Therefore, you cannot proceed. They clapped again. You need to get rid of that way of thinking, man. Read aloud together. Let's go. The greatest commitment of true leadership is to pass on what you have to the next generation. Remember that. That is your greatest obligation. In other words, the success of leadership is measured by the success of your successors.

I am hardly ever home now because I had a replacement assigned to our local service in the Bahamas 15 years ago. That's why I can influence nations and travel all over the world. And until I am here. Leaders understand that every position is temporary. Write this down. Leadership success is measured by what happens in your absence. I repeat. The success of leadership is not measured by what happens in your presence, but by what happens in your absence. If everything stops when you leave, you're a failure.

If people are reading newspapers and talking by the water cooler when you're gone for days, you're a losing and failing leader. If they don't miss you when you leave, you're doing a good job. If things are growing in your absence, you're doing a great job. If I have to remind them of your return, as I always do, it means you're doing a great job. In fact, the greatest act of leadership success is leaving. Jesus proved to be the greatest leader in history because he departed.

What's amazing about this great leader is that his company grew in his absence. Twelve people were left. They became 120. In one week, 3000. And today, 2. 4 billion. He is not present yet. He is still not here. Why? He did a good job. He transferred the tasks. Does anyone here work for that company? I work for the company. I work for the company. Applaud our president. He did a good job. Did you see? I know this is very sad for all of you as Americans, but I'll say it. I'm sure you watched the Olympics.

Three dark-skinned young men from the Bahamas stood there in their beautiful turquoise blue outfits next to the American giants. It was a relay race. It's a relay race. Okay, I want you to remember this for the rest of your lives, okay? Driving is a relay race. Write that down. Engrave it in your minds. It's not a speed race. It's a relay race. Someone was here before you. You have your stage to run, that's all. And now, the moment comes when you must hand over the flag. Driving is not a speed race.

It's a long relay race. I'm sure you noticed during the race that we beat you. I only rub salt into the wound because I feel happy about it. That's okay. It's never okay, really. As you know, so you remember if you watched the race, there was a place where, when they were running, there was a line on the track and another line on the track. That was the space where the runners waited. They were standing behind this last line with their hands like this. Now, between that line and that line they had to pass it.

That was the most important part of the race, not the running. We have lost that. That was the space. The passing area is called the delivery area, and this is where most leaders lose. This is why the church is in chaos today, because most pastors, when they get to this point, cross the point into the other person. They don't want to leave it. He is 90 years old and still wants to preach. What's wrong with you? We continue running, overtaking the other runners. That space, that area, is the key to leadership.

Because it doesn't matter, look, it doesn't matter how fast you are in your phase. If you drop the stick, it doesn't matter if you're in the lead. it's all over. So, it's not about speed. Rather, by passing. Look what she did. I built this. Hallelujah. This entire great program is mine. This is my television program. These are the buses I bought. This is my great work. This is my wipe. These are my miracles. Yes, yes, yes. Then when she dies, a fight breaks out in the meeting room.

The deacons are killing each other. The elders shout, fight, and insult each other. Why? You are a failure. Leadership. It's not about how fast you run. Rather, it depends on how safely you hand over the stick. Do you know what I like about relay races? One person never wins. The whole team wins. Write this down. The key to a relay race is not winning your leg, but passing the baton. I am more concerned about what happens after I die than what happens while I am alive.

Because you could lose everything you've built throughout your life if a foolish person takes over after you. turd. Someone will sell your entire life for a pittance on the altar of self- interest. I don't have time to go into too much detail about the succession, but this is extremely important. It is extremely vital. I have passed by buildings that are now dilapidated. Grass is growing from the window. Because the person who built that empire did not build people to take it over. There's a small phrase here.

The death of leadership. In my book " Passing On," I wrote about a vision I had. I will conclude with this. It is extremely important. I wrote about this vision that I had. I had this vision. I had just finished speaking to about 2000 leaders. I went to the hotel to rest. She lay down on the bed. I don't know if I was asleep or awake at that time. I had a vision. Suddenly I found myself at a funeral. At this funeral, the place was crowded with people, and there was a coffin at the front.

Inside the coffin was a lifeless body. There was a large photograph next to the coffin of the person who had passed away. He was wearing sportswear. What a beautiful picture. It was clear that he was an athlete. And in his hand he was holding a racing baton. Beautiful picture. People were passing by and lining up in front of the coffin. They were crying and wailing and all that follows. Then it was my turn, so I walked around and passed by the coffin.

I looked inside the coffin, and there was a strong, tall, and beautifully groomed athlete, but he was dead and cold. His eyes are closed, and his body is cold. The only problem was that he was holding the racing baton in his hand. Then I woke up drenched in sweat. I asked God, " What does this mean?" He said, " That's a picture of most of my leaders." Cold hands grip the stick like a vise. They would rather die there. The young men are forced to go to the grave to retrieve it because they refused to hand it over.

I have a prayer for you tonight. Die with your hands empty. Let someone come to your funeral with a racing baton in hand, stand over your coffin, smile, and say, " Thank you. I will continue the journey." Yes. Do you know what I consider the greatest and saddest experience in the Civil Rights Movement? We are still looking for the one who took the stick. That's why I'm happy to have you here. That's why I love you so much. He is ready to talk to you. Look, it doesn't matter how great your achievements are.

You must hand over the flag. Leadership is about dying with your hands empty. Which young woman is she working with now to teach her everything she knows? Including your mistakes. Any young man you spend time with and say to him, “My son, I will give you everything I have. For the next two years, just stay with me. Come with me to my home. I want you to see how I deal with my children and how I teach. I want you to go with me on some trips so I can introduce you to the people I meet. I will be your mentor.

I will show you how to make this work.” Who did you embrace? And Jesus said, “ Peter, come here.” Follow me. I will make you become. "In other words, I'm going to make you better than me. Today, we caught fish. I'm going to teach you how to catch people. Stay with me." And they stayed with him. You know, let me conclude with the secret of choosing your successor. This, this, this is Miles's signature style, okay? Because I didn't learn it from any book.

My greatest struggle, I struggled for thirty years asking God: "How do you choose a successor?" "And God has destroyed every concept I had." He amazed me. He broke me. He said: "The goal of leadership is not to keep followers, my son. It is to produce leaders." He said: " True leadership is measured by your success in reducing your followers' dependence on you. In other words, the less they depend on you, my son, the more successful you are." turn. If they need to see you all the time, you're a failure.

If the same long queue at your church every Sunday includes the same people, you should resign. He said to me, "My question to you is, how long should I be with you?" Do you remember that question? They were unable to cast out a demon. The devil did not come out first, but attacked them first. "How long do I have to be with you?" "That was a question about leadership." He would say to them, "Will you learn this quickly, please?" "I want to get out of here." "Stop relying on me."
